question: For the first feasible chained Boolean systems at arity five and six, do four exact unsatisfiable draws per cell refute under fixed-degree MutantXL closure by degree four while two exact satisfiable controls per cell remain unrefuted?

claims.text: Each of the three registered cells receives one exact bounded-four, above-four, draw-dependent, unmeasured, or invalid classification under the preregistered four-unsatisfiable/two-satisfiable rule.
claims.if_supported: Advance bounded cells to growing ell and n, matched external F4, and complete charged cost; retain every other presentation and scale question as open.
claims.if_not_supported: Reject only universal closure degree four at the exact completed cell; degree five and other formulations remain live.

claims.text: No elapsed-time, throughput, end-to-end ECDLP, asymptotic, or cryptographic-scale claim is in scope.

arms.description: First arity-five cell with 43 Boolean variables and 136698 degree-at-most-four columns.
Arity-five cell at the previous measured variable frontier, with 54 variables and 342541 degree-at-most-four columns.
First arity-six cell with 56 variables and 396607 degree-at-most-four columns.
The first two committed natural satisfiable draws in each registered cell; neither XL nor closure may refute them through degree four.
Replay historical m4,n12,ell5,draw24 and require every algebraic counter and closure classification to match the retained row after excluding seconds and source-path spelling.

aa.not_applicable_reason: No clock, throughput, or relative-performance quantity is a metric; all decisions use exact algebraic replay and completion states.

positive.expected_detection: All six controls retain a positive exact solution count and neither XL nor closure refutes at any completely built degree through four.

negative.not_applicable_reason: The exactly-unsatisfiable systems are the registered scientific instances, not a sampled null population; their zero solution counts are checked before closure.

factors.name: source_build_and_caps
factors.value: One frozen commit and release binaries; four threads; degree four; 400000 columns; 32 GB address space.
factors.how: Source, Cargo.lock, commit, binaries, environment, argv, and manifests are hash-bound before new closure data.

factors.name: draw_stream
factors.how: A separate deterministic native generator call per cell; first four exact UNSAT and first two exact SAT records by committed draw index.

factors.name: host
factors.how: Record CPU, memory, kernel, hypervisor, thread count, commit, binaries, and checkpoint segments; these facts cannot license a timing claim.

factors.name: execution_order
factors.value: identity, satisfiable controls, then cells in listed order and ascending draw index
factors.how: One process at a time. Resumes reuse only that draw's checkpoint directory and invalidate wall time.

variable_ledger.aa_not_applicable: No clock or relative-performance comparison is claimed; exact identity and satisfiable controls replace A/A for this algebraic instrument.

randomization.arm_order_reason: Exact computations run one at a time in increasing registered cell and committed draw order; order cannot change algebraic results and no clock is analyzed.

seed_derivation.note: dreg_ladder derives each cell stream from this seed, n, ell, and m; no replacement seed is allowed.

instance_sampling.rule: For each registered cell use the first four exact zero-solution records and first two exact positive-solution records by draw index in the deterministic committed stream; fail the cell gate if unavailable by draw 4095.

blinding.how: All outcomes are exact and the complete fixed sample is reported; no analyst choice or inferential comparison is present.

power.note: This is a finite exact classification of four preregistered UNSAT draws per cell plus two SAT controls, not a population-frequency or significance claim.

preflight_runtime.measured_on: Per-process admission budget only. The complete campaign has 15 sequential processes, each separately capped at 24 hours; no elapsed-time result is analyzed.

primary.name: Exact closure outcome
primary.definition: For an exactly-unsatisfiable draw: closure refutes by degree four, complete degree-four saturation does not refute, or unmeasured because the scan is incomplete/capped/resource-limited.

primary.name: Refuted satisfiable controls
primary.definition: Number of exact positive-solution controls for which XL or closure reports a refutation through a completely built degree four.

primary.name: Historical algebraic identity replay
primary.definition: One iff the m4,n12,ell5,draw24 replay matches every historical algebraic field after excluding seconds, checkpoint segments, and source path.

secondary.name: Closure bit-word operations
secondary.definition: Instrument-emitted closure_word_ops summed over each completely built degree; descriptive work counter only.

secondary.name: Built Boolean monomial columns
secondary.definition: Instrument-emitted exact column count at each completely built degree.

record: Protocol hash, repository commit, source and binary SHA256
Exact argv, environment, cell, draw index, solution count and committed draw SHA256
CPU model, memory bytes, kernel, hypervisor, thread count and placement identity
All JSONL, stderr, exit status, checkpoints and manifest hashes
Every timeout, OOM, cap, invalid control, interruption and resume
Seconds retained as diagnostic only and never interpreted as a metric

stopping_rules.rule: Generate one deterministic stream per cell and select exactly the first four exact UNSAT plus first two exact SAT records by committed draw index; never replace the seed or select by closure outcome.

Run the identity replay and all six satisfiable controls before the twelve UNSAT scans; any algebraic identity mismatch or refuted satisfiable control invalidates scientific interpretation and stops primary execution.

Each process is limited to 400000 columns, 32 billion address-space bytes, four threads, and 86400 seconds. A cap, OOM, timeout, corrupt checkpoint, missing final row, or incomplete degree-four build is unmeasured, never above-four and never a disproof.

invalidation_rules: Any mismatch in the historical identity replay's algebraic fields invalidates the new cells until explained and a new protocol version is filed before rerun.
Any satisfiable control refuted by XL or closure invalidates that cell and the shared instrument; no primary conclusion is allowed.
A draw file generated before the protocol freeze or altered after its commit is inadmissible.
A resumed run whose wall time is interpreted as evidence is inadmissible; exact counters remain usable after manifest-validated restore.

decision_rule.text: Classify each draw only from a complete exact degree-four scan and each cell only after all four UNSAT draws and two SAT controls are measured. Bounded-four requires four of four refutations by degree four; any complete degree-four saturation without refutation rejects universal four at that cell; a mixture is draw-dependent. Any incomplete/resource-limited row makes the cell unmeasured. Controls or identity failures make it invalid.
decision_rule.threshold: Four complete UNSAT draws and two sound SAT controls per cell, plus exact identity replay
decision_rule.statistic: Exact count of closure-by-four versus complete-no-refutation outcomes among four fixed draws per cell
decision_rule.interval: No sampling interval; finite exact registered draws only
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: Exact closure degree category and instrument counters per completed draw; no standardized or timing effect size

graphs: Per-cell exact draw outcomes with unmeasured rows visible
Degree-four columns and closure word-operation counts for complete rows only

inadmissible: Calling timeout, OOM, cap, missing output, incomplete degree, or checkpoint corruption a failure of the mathematical mechanism
Generalizing three toy cells to constant degree at cryptographic scale or to another presentation
Using emitted seconds for a speed, scaling, or comparative claim
Hiding an extra draw, control failure, interrupted row, retry, or resume
Changing the seed, draw selection, cap, degree, or cell after seeing closure output
Closing GG14, FGHR, symmetric, topology-dependent, degree-five, or end-to-end index-calculus leads from this experiment

literature.claim: The three registered m=5,6 cells are the cheapest native high-arity closure discriminator and require four UNSAT draws each on a 32GB host.
The predecessor defines exact draw generation, complete degree-four versus unmeasured classification, and satisfiable soundness replay.
